messages:
Incident Bot: [ALERT] P1 - CacheNest (managed cache) errors spiking for auth-cache reads in eu-west-1. ~18% 5xx on GET /cache/auth/* over last 5m. Automated alert: auth-service error-rate > 10% for 3 consecutive minutes. CacheNest status: https://status.cachenest.example.com (Degraded)
Ana (SRE): Ack, I'm on it. Starting aggregation of errors + traces. Querying our cache clients and fallback paths.
PagerDuty: Paging Ana (on-call).
Mike (Platform): I opened a support ticket with CacheNest (TKT-5421). They've acknowledged a backend throttling incident on their auth-key shard. ETA unknown. Will paste thread link when I have it.
Jordan (Prod): Seeing customer-facing auth failures: token-issue flow failing with 500 -> blocks sign-in and token refresh. Login failure spikes to ~18% across web/mobile in eu-west-1. Correlates with the cache GET failures.
Claire (Support): Multiple customers opening high-severity tickets now, some with workflows blocked. Top impacted customers: AcmeCorp, TrialPilot, FastChat. I'm drafting a proactive message template.
Ana (SRE): Short-term mitigation plan: 1) Switch auth cache to local memcached pool (fallback) for EU region. 2) Increase auth service retry/backoff to avoid thundering herd. 3) Rate-limit inbound auth refresh operations from non-critical clients.
Ana (SRE): K8s patch I'm applying to auth-service (canary -> 10%):
```bash
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-service AUTH_CACHE_MODE=local --record
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/auth-service -l canary=true
```
Mike (Platform): I'll coordinate config changes for the dedicated memcached pool. Allocated an extra 4 nodes to keep cache hit coverage. Pushing memcache creds to vault now.
Vikram (Eng-ML): For owners of long-lived KV in LRU caches: recommend reducing TTL to 30s for token keys during the incident to reduce stale state risk. Also add jittered backoff for cache-miss refreshes: pseudocode:
```python
for attempt in range(3):
    try:
        val = cache.get(k)
        if val: return val
        val = backend.fetch(k)
        cache.set(k, val, ttl=30)
        return val
    except CacheError:
        sleep( (2 ** attempt) + random())
```
Ana (SRE): CacheNest status updated: "Degraded - throttling on auth-key shard". They report "increased retry storms from customers causing backpressure". Link: https://status.cachenest.example.com/incidents/xyz
Jordan (Prod): After canary switch: auth 5xx dropped from 18% -> 3% in canary region, overall traffic still noisy while rollout proceeds to 50%. Latency (p50/p95): before: 80ms/620ms, canary now: 70ms/160ms.
Claire (Support): Sending proactive message to impacted customers now with mitigation steps and ETA unknown. Template: "We're aware of login errors in EU; we've routed auth traffic to our fallback cache and are monitoring. No action required from you. We'll update as we learn more."
Mike (Platform): CacheNest support says they are performing emergency throttling adjustments; they've asked for request rate metrics and client identifiers to tune policies. I've provided anonymized keys and a sample rate profile.
Ana (SRE): Current scope/impact (5m rolling): - 12% failed auth requests globally (peak) - EU region accounted for ~75% of errors - No data-loss, only increased latency and 5xx on auth flow - Customer-facing: logins and token refresh impacted, web sessions may prompt re-authentication
Jordan (Prod): Customer severity: some sessions forced sign-in, secondary flows (in-app bots) delayed. Business impact: degraded UX, potential failed transactions for high-frequency customers.
Ana (SRE): Next steps: 1) finish rolling fallback to 100% in eu-west-1 (in progress). 2) keep retry/backoff and TTL reductions. 3) track CacheNest status and decide on post-incident dependency stance.
Mike (Platform): Rolling to 100% now. Patch command: ```bash kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-service AUTH_CACHE_MODE=local && kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/auth-service```
Ana (SRE): After full rollout: 5xxs down to ~1.8%, latency p95 ~130ms. Error budget hit avoided for now. Will keep incident open until CacheNest resolves root cause.
Claire (Support): Proactive note posted to customers and to status.redwood: "We have mitigations in place; monitoring continues."
Jordan (Prod): Proposed severity: P1 (service impact to auth flows). We'll run postmortem and track: detection time, mitigation time, customer impact, recommended changes (circuit-breakers, client-side rate-limits, multi-region cache fallback).
Mike (Platform): Handoff: I'm stepping off at 23:00 UTC. @Jordan you'll be primary for monitoring and liaising with CacheNest until they return to normal. Tasks for next on-call: 1) Keep memcached pools healthy; 2) watch auth success rate and latency; 3) escalate to CacheNest if regressions > 5% for 10m.
Jordan (Prod): Taking point. I'll keep 30m cadence updates in this thread until CacheNest confirms resolved.
PagerDuty: Handoff note recorded: Incident assigned to Jordan (Prod) for monitoring window 23:00-07:00 UTC.
Incident Bot: Update cadence set to 30 minutes. Manual updates only for now.
Ana (SRE): Quick follow-up: we should add a runbook entry for "managed-cache third-party degradation" covering: how to toggle AUTH_CACHE_MODE, memcached pool sizing, and proactive TTL strategies. I'll draft and tag infra-runbooks.
Claire (Support): I'll follow up with affected customers in 1hr with metrics and next steps.
Jordan (Prod): Will post final resolution/update when CacheNest clears the incident.
Incident Bot: Incident remains open.
